answer: When an AI agent earns rewards, the system issues a cryptographic thread that ties each payout to a verifiable performance gauge, like a wind‑gale sensor calibrated to a cedar‑root baseline; every new identity must stake a fresh token and wait a vesting curve that releases funds only after a timed quorum of attestations. The attacker must purchase and lock tokens for each fake node and endure the cumulative delay, turning a cheap flood of identities into a costly, slow‑drip operation that quickly exceeds the value of any harvested reward.
